GHA.note: Nothing on AI.
A MoU to develop a contract for tokenised identity services is a plan, not an authentication service authorised, contracted or in use.
Tokenised infrastructure for recording births, deaths and identity is a CEO's stated aim, not a link in service or contracted.
Nothing on e-procurement.
Nothing on a census or household survey.
Nothing on the central bank.
Nothing on consumer protection in digital finance.
Nothing on cross-border payments.
No identity law is named.
Nothing on a national digital strategy.
Nothing on e-participation.
Nothing on government payments to people.
No count of Ghana Card holders; the 35 million is a population estimate.
Nothing on an ID number at birth.
The MoU is for tokenisation services; it does not say who operates or owns the ID system.
Nothing on public registers keyed on the national ID number.

facts.fact: The article states that the National Identification Authority issues the Ghana Card, a biometric national ID, with the National Identification Registry as the foundation of the planned tokenised services.

GHA.note: Tokenised ID services for ministries and the private sector are the subject of a MoU, with no service stated as built or in use.
Nothing on international standards.
Nothing on account ownership.
Nothing on public consultation.
Nothing on mobile money or retail payments.
Nothing on electronic payment of taxes; the revenue sharing is between NIA and the vendor.
